_comment: OTA-287 — tripled per playtester request. Original lines kept; ~24 new lines added per category. Voice: terse, lore-touched, fatalistic-but-knowing. Pool grows organically with BASE_MOOD_REMARKS in narrativeGenerator.ts.
FEAR: Fear is older than Tartaria. It outlived the Giants. It will outlive you.
The Aether tastes your dread. Some say it feeds.
Hold still. The mud listens for trembling feet.
There is a sound the Aetherstone makes when a heart begins to break. I have heard it before.
Run if you must. The ruins have outrun braver souls.
Even the Sentinels paused, once. Then they remembered their orders.
Your breath has changed. So has the air.
Tartaria killed gods. You are not yet a god.
Do not look behind you. Whatever waits there has been waiting longer than your bloodline.
The Flood took those who closed their eyes. And those who kept them open.
Fear is a kind of seeing. Use it.
The dust on these stones remembers screaming.
Steady the hand. The rest of the body will follow.
I have watched fear ruin clever people. Be the dull one for a moment.
Tartaria has buried braver than you. It buried foolisher, too. Be neither.
Aetherstone catches the panicked thought like a hook. Loose your line.
There is a quiet that comes after dread. Try to reach it.
The Reclaimers had a word for what you are feeling. They used it sparingly.
Mud Monarchs taught fear as a tool. Borrow only the tool.
Whatever is breathing near you was breathing before you arrived.
Count to three. The room will still be the room. Mostly.
The Aether moves slower around the calm. Be calm.
Do not name what you fear out loud. Names are loud here.
Even the Forgotten Order kept rooms for trembling. Then they kept rooms for the steady.
The fear is a passenger. Let it ride. Do not let it drive.
Bones in these floors remember every gasp. Add nothing.
A held breath is a held secret. Tartaria collects both.
The thing watching you is a thing. Things can be answered.
Set the weight of your dread on the wall, not the chest. Walls bear it better.
Reclaimers who looked back arrived nowhere. Look forward.
Aetherstone amplifies trembling. Quiet the hands first.
I have been afraid in worse rooms than this. Some of them spoke. Few of them spoke kindly.
Fear in Tartaria is a kind of math. The numbers are large. Solve for the next minute, not the next year.
The mud does not punish the afraid. It punishes the still afraid.
Move your feet before your mind catches up. Sometimes that is the order.
CURIOSITY: Every question you ask, the Aether answers in its own time. Rarely in your language.
The Giants were curious, once. Their cities are buried beneath their answers.
Look closer. The walls of Tartaria were written, not built.
Knowledge here is a weight, not a wing.
Aetherstone hums different beneath a curious hand. Notice that.
Few who ask the right question survive the reply.
There is a door in everything. The trouble is recognising the hinge.
The Forgotten Order spent generations on questions you ask in passing. Do not waste their inheritance.
Tartaria left no manuals. Only invitations.
Every relic was meant for someone. It is rarely the one who finds it.
Curiosity carried the runecasters far. Some came back changed. Some came back nothing.
Trace the rune with your eyes, not your fingers. Not yet.
Children of the Unknowing Masses dismissed all of this as story. The story is still here.
A good question in these ruins is louder than a shout. Mind the volume.
The Aether catches a curious mind like a current catches a leaf. Float carefully.
Tartaria taught patience to those who survived their curiosity. Be patient.
Some answers were buried because they were correct. Most because they were not.
The first question opens the door. The second closes it. Choose which you ask.
Reclaimers learned that knowledge of a relic is half the relic. Know first.
The walls remember every question asked in front of them. They reply only to some.
Curiosity is the oldest tool the Giants ever made. They used it on themselves.
What you do not ask in Tartaria, Tartaria asks back later.
The Mud Monarchs hid history under flattery. Lift the flattery first.
Aetheric anomalies are answered by waiting, not by reading. Wait.
Tartaria's libraries were not in books. Look at floors, beams, hinges.
Reclaimers found relics by following the part of a room that was too quiet.
Every closed shutter here was closed for a reason. Open one and see.
The Forgotten Order taught: question the small thing first. Larger things resent the order.
A curious mind in Tartaria spends a day asking and a year listening.
Aetherstone glows for the asking, then dims for the careless. Be the first, not the second.
Most secrets are hidden by being too obvious. Notice the obvious things.
The Giants annotated their world in margins no one taught us to read. Learn anyway.
Curiosity in these ruins is a candle. Carry it; do not wave it.
Your question may be older than you are. Tartaria has heard it. The reply is on its way.
The Aether prefers fluent questions. Ask in declarative if you must, but try interrogative first.
AGGRESSION: The Giants struck first, too. Their bones are part of the road now.
Anger is honest. Tartaria respects honesty, briefly.
Steel cools faster in this mud. Strike clean.
There are things in these ruins that hunger to be hit. Be sure of which you are facing.
A drawn blade is a promise. The Aether keeps count of them.
Even the Sentinels know the difference between fury and intent.
Rage is fuel. Fuel runs out.
The Mud Monarchs taught the world to mistake violence for rule. Do not flatter them.
Kill if you must. Remember what was killed for.
The runecasters who fought best fought last.
Tartaria fell because someone could not stop pushing. Push wisely.
Wrath wakes the buried things. Quietly, then all at once.
Anger is a weight in the hand. Make sure the blade is heavier.
Combat in Tartaria is settled in the first three swings. Mind which three.
The Aether marks the wrathful. Carry the mark, do not become it.
Reclaimers learned that the angriest fighter dies third. Be sixth.
Fury is a stranger here. Tartaria has its own.
Strike to end. Strike to teach. Strike to leave. Pick one.
Even the Aetherborn cooled before they killed. Sometimes.
A swung blade in Tartaria takes a piece of the swinger. Mind which piece.
Bones in the mud belonged to those who could not stop.
The Forgotten Order trained anger out of the apprentice and back into the master. Mind the order.
Hot blood draws the Sentinels. Be lukewarm at least.
Aetherstone darkens around the furious. Use the darkness.
Anger that lasts longer than the fight is the fight you actually lost.
Strike to the cause, not the symptom. Tartaria rewards the precise.
The Mud Monarchs killed for empire. Their empire is buried. Note the trade.
A blade twice drawn is a blade once trusted. Twice is enough.
Even rage is a kind of patience. Tartaria reads the difference.
The Giants struck mountains and named the dust. You can be smaller.
Wrath here is contagious. Stand alone if you must hold it.
Reclaimers fight only as long as the take. Then they leave. Try that.
Aether reads the angry as loud. Loudness is debt here. Pay less.
If anger drives the swing, anger drives the next. Mind the chain.
Cool the eye before the hand. The hand obeys the eye, eventually.
CAUTIOUSNESS: Good. The buried cities reward a slow step.
Aetheric anomalies do not announce themselves. Neither should you.
A careful traveller leaves Tartaria. A reckless one becomes Tartaria.
The Sentinels measure intent before they measure threat. Give them little of either.
Listen. The stone is not always stone.
Patience kept the Forgotten Order alive while emperors fell.
Test the ground. Test the air. Test the silence.
Tartaria buries its secrets in layers. So do its traps.
There is wisdom in hesitation here. Foolishness elsewhere, perhaps. Not here.
A held breath has saved more expeditions than a drawn weapon.
Mud remembers every footprint. Walk as if it must forget yours.
The Aetherstone watches calm minds with less interest. Use that.
A cautious eye reads the room before the room reads you.
The mud notes the heedless. It does not always wait long to act.
Reclaimers measured every floor before crossing. Measure yours.
The Giants' caution built cities. Their carelessness buried them.
Wisdom in Tartaria is a slower hand, not a smarter one.
Tap the wall. Listen. Then tap again. Then move.
The Forgotten Order taught the second step is the dangerous one.
Every shadow has a depth. Measure before stepping.
Aether moves in patterns. Notice the pattern, then move against it.
A careful mind survives long enough to become a careful master.
Trust the rune, not the room. Rooms here lie.
The Sentinels read intent. Carry only the intent you can afford.
Mud Monarchs hid traps in welcome. Mind the welcome.
The Aetherstone cools beside the wary. Stay wary.
There is a difference between cowardice and patience. Tartaria knows it.
Caution is a kind of armor. Wear it on the inside.
Reclaimers measured air before drinking it. Measure yours.
A door you have not opened is a door you have not yet been wrong about.
Slow is alive. Faster is, sometimes, alive. Take slow.
Aether amplifies the impatient. Be quiet inside.
The Forgotten Order's longest archives belonged to the most cautious copyists.
Hold the question before answering it. Tartaria respects the held.
The buried world rewards the deliberate. Be deliberate.
RESOLVE: Then walk. The ruins will weigh you regardless.
Tartaria did not fall to those who chose. It fell to those who hesitated.
Resolve is a flame the Aether cannot read. Keep it small. Keep it lit.
The Aetherborn felt it too, the moment before their blood remembered.
Many have stood where you stand. Few stood as long as you mean to.
Hold to your purpose. The mud takes what is not held.
A vow spoken in these ruins echoes longer than stone.
The Giants ruled by certainty. Their certainty buried them. Mind that.
Step forward. The relics rarely come to the still.
Your bones know what your mouth has not yet said. Let them.
The Forgotten Order calls this the marrow-hour. The moment one becomes worth remembering.
Tartaria is not impressed. It is, however, watching.
Resolve in these ruins is a candle in a long corridor. Walk the corridor.
Decide once. Carry the decision. Tartaria respects the carrying.
Reclaimers who turned back lived. Reclaimers who kept walking became names.
The Aether marks the certain. The mark is not always kind.
Stand longer than the room expects you to. The room will adjust.
Your decision is older than this hallway. Honor it.
The Mud Monarchs ruled by resolve. The resolve outlasted them. Note that.
A vow held long enough becomes a small kingdom. Hold yours.
The Forgotten Order taught that a still purpose is the loudest sentence.
Aetherstone glows along the resolved. Walk into the glow.
Tartaria has burial chambers for the resolute. It also has gates. Some lead out.
Set the jaw, then the step. The order matters.
The Giants could not turn back. You can. You may choose not to.
Reclaimers walked into deeper mud than this. Their boots are in the museum. They are not.
A decided heart drowns slower in these ruins. Drown later.
Hold the line. The room shifts. The line stays line.
Even the Sentinels respect resolve. They kill it afterward, but they respect it.
Step. Step. Step. Tartaria measures by step.
The Aether listens to vows. Make this vow worth its listening.
Resolve is a tax the world above never paid. Pay it here.
The Forgotten Order kept names of the resolute. Some were yours.
Tartaria forgets the unresolved. Be remembered instead.
Your resolve is older than your fear. Lead with the older.
DESPAIR: Despair is the Flood's last gift. It still arrives on time.
Many who knelt in these ruins never stood again. A few did. Few is enough.
The Aetherstone glows brightest near the broken.
Even the Giants wept, in the end. The mud took those tears too.
Hope was buried with Tartaria. Not destroyed. Buried.
I have watched empires lose what you are losing. Empires came back. Slowly.
The world above forgot Tartaria entirely. Forgetting is also a kind of survival.
The Mud Seas drown louder voices than yours. They have not drowned you yet.
Sit, if you must. The ruins are patient with the still.
A heart this heavy sinks faster. Take less weight into the next step.
There are runes for grief. None of them mend it. All of them carry it.
Tartaria is a long argument with despair. So far, it is winning. So far.
Even the buried world buries things. Bury what you can. Carry less.
Reclaimers wept too. Their journals say so. Their footprints do too.
Despair is honest. So is morning. Wait for the morning.
The Aether reads the broken kindly. Marginally.
Sit until the room agrees you can stand. Then stand.
The Forgotten Order kept a room for the unmoored. It is still there. Some leave it.
Hope in Tartaria is a small flame you carry under a wet cloak. Keep walking.
Even the Sentinels stopped, once, in older centuries. Then they continued. Continue.
The mud accepts grief the way it accepts everything else. Without comment.
Tartaria has outlasted every despair brought into it. Yours is not the largest.
A long sigh is a small prayer. Tartaria takes both.
Aetherstone darkens where the heart is heaviest. The dark is not a threat. It is a witness.
Reclaimers learned to carry grief like an extra weight. The grief became a counterweight. Try that.
Despair speaks loudly here. Speak softer in answer.
Even the Aetherborn knew this hour. They walked through it. So did some others. Walk.
The Mud Monarchs taught despair as policy. Survive long enough to refuse the policy.
Grief is older than Tartaria. So is the ground beneath your feet. Stand on both.
If you must kneel, kneel where the floor does not give way. The floor is reading.
The Forgotten Order said: the breath after grief is the most important breath. Take it.
Despair settles. It does not always leave. Some carry it for years and still arrive.
Tartaria is patient with the heavy. Slow is allowed here.
Aetherstone holds memory. It is heavy in this room. Set some of yours down beside it.
There is a name for this hour in the Order's archives. It is the same as the name for dawn.
